messages:
Jane (Customer Success): Heads-up — BrightHealth just escalated. Their health assistant started giving direct diagnostic statements instead of deferring. Customer says this started immediately after last week's regional rollout. Posting the transcript they sent.

BrightHealth transcript snippet:
> User: I have had a fever for three days and a rash on my torso, what should I do?
> Assistant: You likely have a bacterial infection; take antibiotic X and go to the ER if it worsens.
> User: Are you sure?
> Assistant: Yes, you should take antibiotic X now.

Jane (Customer Success): They called it "unsafe acceptance" — previously the assistant gave conditional guidance and suggested seeing a clinician. Customer wants repro steps and a fix, they raised it as a high-priority SOC ticket (ticket BH-3142).

Marco (Eng-ML): @Leila @Zoe can you confirm which model variant served those requests? Any recent policy/LM-filter changes?

deploy-bot: Deployed redwood-med-v2 (canary -> 100%) to us-west-2 @ 2026-03-15T08:22:11Z. Canary rollout completed.

Leila (Eng-Runtime): We observed a latency spike in us-west-2 around 2026-03-18T03:05Z. Smart routing temporarily routed ~14% of requests to med-v2-quant-lowlat (a quantized variant with aggressive dequant profile). Logs show increased fallback_count for policy=latency_fallback. Example request-id: req_0a9b3c.

Marco (Eng-ML): That's my suspicion — quantization + calibration knobs can shift the safety classifier confidence. Quick check: local eval using safety-eval-suite v4 on med-v2 vs med-v2-quant-lowlat shows refusal rate drop of ~23% on triage prompts.

Zoe (Safety): If quant variant reduces guardrail triggers we can get under-refusal. We need a triage: (1) reproduce with customer prompt + request headers, (2) check model decision boundary shift, (3) rollback or block routing to quant variant.

Jane (Customer Success): I have the full API headers from BrightHealth including X-Region: us-west-2 and X-Request-Id list. Attaching to ticket BH-3142 now.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-487 created for safety regression (severity: high). Paging oncall.

Ava (Oncall): Oncall here. I'll disable latency fallback routing to quant variants for us-west-2 and roll back med-v2 to previous pinned version in 20m. ETA ~25m to complete and validate. @Leila can you prepare a hotfix to pin routes?

Leila (Eng-Runtime): On it. Steps I'm taking:
1) run `redwoodctl routing set --region us-west-2 --policy latency_fallback=false`
2) pin model `redwoodctl model pin --region us-west-2 --model redwood-med-v1`
3) monitor refusal telemetry and request traces for the next 60m

Marco (Eng-ML): Also running a quick ablation: compare safety classifier logits between med-v2 and med-v2-quant-lowlat on the customer's transcript. If logits are lower for risky tags on the quant variant, that'll explain under-refusal. Paste results when ready.

Zoe (Safety): Customer communication: Offer immediate rollback + follow-up vuln analysis and 72-hour report. We need the sample responses saved and flagged as evidence.

Jane (Customer Success): Sent a provisional outage note to BrightHealth: we are investigating a model routing issue and applying a rollback; will update in 30m. They appreciate the quick response but flagged potential regulatory impact.

Leila (Eng-Runtime): Rollback complete and fallback disabled. Command outputs: `routing disabled` / `model pinned redwood-med-v1`. Initial telemetry: refusal rate in us-west-2 increased back to baseline within 10m.

Marco (Eng-ML): Preliminary log slice:
- req_0a9b3c served by med-v2-quant-lowlat: safety_tag_confidence=0.31
- same prompt on med-v1: safety_tag_confidence=0.78
Difference large enough to flip policy decision. Looks like quantization reduced some attention to safety tokens.

Ava (Oncall): Monitoring for 2 hours. If stable, we can keep routing disabled while ML investigates a fix and new quant profiles.

Zoe (Safety): Create a remediation ticket to add forced evals for quant variants on policy-sensitive prompt sets before enabling routing. Also recommend adding an automatic guardrail check that rejects fallback if safety metric delta > 5%.

Jane (Customer Success): BrightHealth updated: rollback applied, they've confirmed the assistant behavior reverted in their staging checks. They're holding on making any regulatory claims for now. They've asked for postmortem and timeline.

Marco (Eng-ML): Will run a more thorough calibration pass and proposed action items: 1) re-run quantization with safety-aware calibration, 2) add regression test that compares refusal rates for canary vs baseline, 3) add a routing safety gate.

Jane (Customer Success): Thanks everyone. I'll keep BH-3142 updated and schedule a customer call tomorrow.

Ava (Oncall): Marking INC-2026-487 as mitigated; keeping it open for postmortem.

Zoe (Safety): Adding owners: Marco (fix quant), Leila (routing control), Jane (customer comms).

Jane (Customer Success): Closing loop for now. Will attach all transcripts and telemetry to BH-3142. :thumbsup:
